# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_config_doc.py from src/jarvis/config.py and config.example.toml.
     Do not edit by hand: run `uv run python scripts/gen_config_doc.py` after changing either file. -->

This page lists every setting in `config.toml`: its type, its default and what it does. It is generated
from the configuration model in `src/jarvis/config.py` and the comments in `config.example.toml`.

- **`config.toml`** is your configuration, in the Jarvis folder. `jarvis setup` creates it from
  `config.example.toml` (with the comments) and, when it already exists, only adds the keys it lacks.
  The file is personal and ignored by git.
- **`config.local.toml`** is optional and sits next to `config.toml`. It is merged over `config.toml` when
  Jarvis loads: tables merge key by key; every other value, arrays and arrays of tables included, replaces
  the value from `config.toml`. Use it for values that should stay out of a shared `config.toml`.
- **Secrets never go into a config file.** API keys and tokens live in the macOS Keychain
  (`jarvis key set NAME`).
- **Default** is the value Jarvis uses when the key is missing. **Example** is the value that
  `config.example.toml` (and so a new `config.toml`) sets, shown only when it differs from the default.
  A key marked *required* has no default and must be present.
- Unknown keys are an error, so a typo is reported instead of being ignored. `jarvis doctor` checks the file.

## [general]

- **`language`** (`"en" | "tr"`; default: `"en"`): "en" | "tr": the main language (`jarvis setup --language`); replies follow the language of your latest message
- **`language_default`** (string; default: `""`; **deprecated**, use `general.language` instead): the key before `language`; still read (as `language`) and flagged by `jarvis doctor`
- **`log_level`** (`"DEBUG" | "INFO" | "WARNING" | "ERROR"`; default: `"DEBUG"`; example: `"INFO"`): "DEBUG" writes much more into logs/jarvis.log
- **`save_transcripts`** (boolean; default: `true`): full transcripts into SQLite
- **`use_voice`** (boolean; default: `false`): true lets `jarvis voice` (the hands-free service) start
- **`exit_words`** (list of strings, at least 1 entry; default: `["exit", "quit", "bye"]`): the chat exits when the whole input is exactly one of these (Ctrl-D too)

## [persona]

How Jarvis talks (prompts/persona.&lt;language>.md, or your own data/persona.md). `humor_level` picks the frequency-and-style block that the persona's [[HUMOR]] marker expands to: 0 = none, 1 = light (now and then), 2 = playful (a quip in most casual replies, the default), 3 = very playful (every casual reply, bolder teasing). The persona's own exceptions (failures, serious topics, confirmations, hurry) hold at every level.

How much Jarvis jokes (the persona, src/jarvis/prompts/persona.&lt;language>.md or data/persona.md): 0 = none, 1 = light (a friendly remark now and then), 2 = playful (a short quip or tease after the answer in most casual replies), 3 = very playful (every casual reply, bolder teasing). The answer always comes first and correct; failures, serious topics, confirmations of risky actions and "acelem var" get no joke at any level.

- **`humor_level`** (integer, 0 to 3; default: `2`)

## [memory]

Long-term memory (data/memory.md) beyond an explicit "remember this".

data/memory.md is written when you say "remember this" ("bunu hatırla") and, with auto = true, also when you state something durable about yourself (a preference, a routine, a person, a place you go often, a project, a plan with a date). Never from emails, web pages or sheets unless you ask. A fact that updates an old one replaces the old line.

- **`auto`** (boolean; default: `true`): the model calls `remember` on its own for durable facts the user states about themselves
- **`auto_notify`** (boolean; default: `true`): a "📝 Noted: …" line in the terminal and on Telegram when something is saved on its own (voice: only logged)
- **`end_of_session_pass`** (boolean; default: `true`): when a session ends (exit, the daily rollover, a quiet gap) one cheap call proposes facts the conversation missed
- **`idle_pass_min`** (integer, >= 0; default: `30`): the pass also runs for the turns before a gap of this many quiet minutes (0 = never)
- **`max_facts_per_pass`** (integer, 1 to 20; default: `5`)

## [models]

- **`main_model`** (string; *required*; example: `"claude-sonnet-5-5"`)
- **`delegate_model`** (string; *required*; example: `"claude-sonnet-5-5"`)
- **`main_thinking`** (boolean; default: `false`): Current models use adaptive thinking: there is no token budget, only an effort level (low | medium | high | xhigh | max). With thinking off, effort must be high or lower.
- **`main_effort`** (`"low" | "medium" | "high" | "xhigh" | "max"`; default: `"medium"`)
- **`delegate_thinking`** (boolean; default: `true`)
- **`delegate_effort`** (`"low" | "medium" | "high" | "xhigh" | "max"`; default: `"high"`)
- **`max_output_tokens`** (integer, >= 1; default: `1024`): Thinking tokens count against max_output_tokens. When thinking is on, Jarvis raises the effective cap to at least 4096 so that reasoning cannot swallow the whole reply.
- **`delegate_max_output_tokens`** (integer, >= 1; default: `4096`)

## [loop]

The Claude API loop. The timeouts are granular, never one short total limit: the SDK default of 5 s to connect (TCP + TLS) is too short on a slow network, while a long answer must never be cut. `api_connect_timeout_s` covers the TCP connect and the TLS handshake; `api_read_timeout_s` is the longest silence allowed between two chunks of the stream (a stalled stream), so a healthy long answer is never cut while a dead connection is noticed.

- **`max_tool_iterations`** (integer, >= 1; default: `10`): per turn, hard cap
- **`api_max_attempts`** (integer, >= 1; default: `3`): retries for API errors, then raise JarvisAPIError
- **`api_backoff_base_seconds`** (number, > 0; default: `1.0`)
- **`api_connect_timeout_s`** (number, > 0, <= 120; default: `10.0`): Granular API timeouts (no short total limit). connect = TCP + TLS handshake (the SDK default of 5 s is too short on a slow network). read = the longest silence allowed between two chunks of the streamed reply (a stalled stream), not the length of the whole answer. write = sending the request body.
- **`api_read_timeout_s`** (number, > 0, <= 600; default: `60.0`): max silence between stream events
- **`api_write_timeout_s`** (number, > 0, <= 600; default: `60.0`): sending the request body

## [context]

- **`compact_after_tokens`** (integer, >= 1; default: `30000`): when the conversation (not the system prompt and tool schemas, ~28k tokens on their own) exceeds this, summarize older turns
- **`keep_recent_turns`** (integer, >= 0; default: `6`): always keep the last N turns verbatim (at least 1; a reply that asked a question is never summarized away from its answer)
- **`tool_result_max_chars`** (integer, >= 100; default: `12000`): truncate any single tool result above this
- **`resume_after_min`** (integer, >= 0; default: `15`): a new session (restart, midnight rollover, another interface) replays the last turns of these minutes as text; 0 = off

## [budget]

- **`daily_budget_usd`** (number, >= 0; default: `3.0`)
- **`warn_at_fraction`** (number, 0 to 1; default: `0.8`): warn at 80%
- **`cache_read_multiplier`** (number, >= 0; default: `0.1`): cache reads cost this fraction of the input price
- **`cache_write_multiplier`** (number, >= 0; default: `1.25`): 5-minute cache writes cost this multiple of the input price
- **`elevenlabs_usd_per_1k_chars`** (number, >= 0; default: `0.22`): Estimated prices of the other paid services, only for the dashboard's cost charts. VERIFY against your plans: ElevenLabs charges per character of a monthly quota, Google Maps per request. Creator plan: $22 per 100k characters
- **`maps_usd_per_call`** (number, >= 0; default: `0.005`): about $5 per 1000 Places / Directions requests
- **`prices`**: see [`[budget.prices."NAME"]`](#budgetpricesname).

### [budget.prices."NAME"]

A table of tables: each `"NAME" = { ... }` line under `[budget.prices]` is one entry.

USD per million tokens.

Prices are per million tokens. VERIFY against current Anthropic pricing before use.

- **`input`** (number, >= 0; *required*; example: `0.1`)
- **`output`** (number, >= 0; *required*; example: `0.5`)

## [calendar]

- **`default_write_calendar`** (`"google" | "apple"`; default: `"google"`): "google" or "apple"
- **`apple_calendar_exclude`** (list of strings; default: `[]`): names of Apple calendars to skip on read (e.g. a Google account already synced into macOS Calendar)
- **`filters`**: see [`[[calendar.filters]]`](#calendarfilters).

### [[calendar.filters]]

An array of tables: each `[[calendar.filters]]` block in the file adds one entry.

One `[[calendar.filters]]` entry: in the calendar named `calendar`, show only the events whose title contains one of `keywords` (case- and Turkish-accent-insensitive; a keyword of up to three characters such as "FB" only as a whole word). With `only_matches` (default) the filter applies only to fixture-shaped titles ("A - B", "A vs B"); other entries in that calendar stay visible.

- **`calendar`** (string, at least 1 character; *required*; example: `"Futbol"`)
- **`mode`** (`"include_only"`; default: `"include_only"`)
- **`keywords`** (list of strings, at least 1 entry; *required*; example: `["Fenerbahçe", "Fenerbahce", "Fener", "FB"]`)
- **`only_matches`** (boolean; default: `true`)

## [weather]

Where "what's the weather" is for when no place is named. `current`: the Current Location, falling back to the home Location of profile.md and then to `fixed_location`; `home`: always the profile's Location; `fixed`: always `fixed_location`. `default_location` is the older name of `fixed_location`: it is still read as `fixed_location` (`jarvis doctor` warns).

Where "what's the weather" is for when no place is named: "current" = the Current Location detected at session start (Shortcut > CoreLocationCLI > IP), then the home `Location` line of data/profile.md, then fixed_location "home" = always the profile's Location; "fixed" = always fixed_location `default_location` was the key before this release; it is still read (as fixed_location) and `jarvis doctor` warns.

- **`location_source`** (`"current" | "home" | "fixed"`; default: `"current"`)
- **`fixed_location`** (string; default: `""`): `jarvis setup` fills it from your home location
- **`default_location`** (string; default: `""`; **deprecated**, use `weather.fixed_location` and `weather.location_source` instead)

## [security]

- **`allowed_file_roots`** (list of strings, at least 1 entry; *required*; example: `["~/Documents", "~/Desktop", "~/Downloads", "~/Developer"]`)
- **`denied_paths`** (list of strings; *required*; example: `["~/.ssh", "~/.gnupg", "~/.aws", "~/Library/Keychains", "~/.config/gcloud"]`)
- **`shell_denylist`** (list of strings; *required*; example: `["sudo", "rm -rf /", "rm -fr /", "rm -r -f /", "rm -f -r /", "mkfs", "dd if=", ":(){", "chmod -R 777 /", "curl * | sh", "wget * | sh", "curl * | bash", "wget * | bash", "curl * | zsh", "wget * | zsh", "security find-generic-password", "security find-internet-password", "security dump-keychain"]`): Matched (with * as a wildcard) against the command text and the parsed argv. Confirmation is the real control; this list only refuses the obviously destructive, including the rm/curl variants and `security` reads of the Keychain (which holds the API key).
- **`shell_timeout_seconds`** (integer, >= 1; default: `60`)

## [logging]

- **`app_log_retention_days`** (integer, >= 1; default: `14`)
- **`audit_log_retention_days`** (integer, >= 1; default: `90`)

## [screen]

- **`max_image_side_px`** (integer, 256 to 8000; default: `1568`): screenshots are downscaled to this longest side before the model sees them
- **`store_images`** (boolean; default: `false`): true keeps screenshot bytes in the SQLite transcript; false stores only a reference

## [training]

- **`health_inbox`** (string; default: `"~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Jarvis/health_inbox"`)
- **`sync_on_startup`** (boolean; default: `true`): import new Health files from the inbox when Jarvis starts

## [timers]

- **`notification_sound`** (string; default: `"Glass"`)
- **`notify_channels`** (list of `"mac" | "telegram"`; default: `["mac"]`): add "telegram" once the Telegram bot is set up
- **`pomodoro_work_min`** (integer, >= 1; default: `25`)
- **`pomodoro_break_min`** (integer, >= 1; default: `5`)
- **`pomodoro_long_break_min`** (integer, >= 1; default: `15`)
- **`pomodoro_cycles`** (integer, >= 1; default: `4`)

## [alarm]

Alarms (tools/alarms.py): a loud, looping sound on the Mac at a clock time, stopped or snoozed from a dialog, the push-to-talk hotkey, a spoken word or Telegram, with a phone backup so a wake-up alarm also reaches the iPhone. Timers (`[timers]`) are the "N minutes from now" notifications.

Alarms ("set an alarm for 7 am"): a loud looping sound on the Mac with a Stop / Snooze dialog; "remind me in N minutes" stays a timer ([timers] above). sounds/alarm.m4a (or .mp3/.wav/.aiff) is the sound; without it a macOS system sound loops. The system volume is raised to `volume` while it rings and restored afterwards.

- **`sound`** (string; default: `"alarm"`): sounds/alarm.m4a|.mp3|.wav|.aiff (first found); a macOS system sound when missing
- **`sound_volume`** (number, 0.0 to 2.0; default: `1.0`): `afplay -v` gain on top of the system volume
- **`volume`** (integer, 0 to 100; default: `70`): the system output volume while ringing; restored afterwards
- **`max_ring_min`** (integer, 1 to 60; default: `10`): the alarm stops by itself after this
- **`snooze_min`** (integer, 1 to 60; default: `9`): "Ertele" and `snooze_alarm` without minutes
- **`keep_awake_hours`** (integer, 0 to 48; default: `12`): caffeinate keeps the Mac from idle sleep while an alarm is due within this window
- **`low_battery_percent`** (integer, 0 to 100; default: `20`): on battery below this (or with the lid closed) setting an alarm warns that it may not ring
- **`phone_backup`** (`"reminder" | "telegram" | "both" | "off"`; default: `"both"`): Phone backup so a wake-up alarm also reaches the iPhone: "reminder" (an Apple Reminder in the list below, synced through iCloud; a normal timed reminder, not an alarm-style one), "telegram" (a message at the alarm time), "both", "off".
- **`reminder_list`** (string; default: `"Jarvis Alarm"`): the Reminders list that holds the backups (created when missing)

## [football]

- **`team`** (string; default: `"Fenerbahçe"`)
- **`league`** (string; default: `"Süper Lig"`)
- **`provider`** (string; default: `"api-football"`): The API key is OPTIONAL: football questions are answered by web_search first. Without a key the football.* tools are not offered to the model at all (`jarvis key set football_api_key` enables them). API-Football (api-sports.io)
- **`cache_ttl_fixtures_min`** (integer, >= 1; default: `360`)
- **`cache_ttl_standings_min`** (integer, >= 1; default: `60`)
- **`cache_ttl_live_min`** (integer, >= 1; default: `1`)

## [telegram]

- **`enabled`** (boolean; default: `false`)
- **`allowed_user_id`** (integer; default: `0`): your numeric Telegram user id (`jarvis telegram whoami`)
- **`allowed_chat_id`** (integer; default: `0`): your private chat id with the bot (`jarvis telegram whoami`)
- **`confirm_timeout_min`** (integer, >= 1; default: `5`)
- **`max_messages_per_minute`** (integer, >= 1; default: `20`)
- **`poll_timeout_s`** (integer, 1 to 50; default: `30`)
- **`remote_allowed_tools`** (list of strings; default: `[]`; example: `["calendar_merged.agenda", "google_calendar.google_list_events", "google_calendar.google_create_event", "apple_calendar.apple_list_events", "apple_reminders.list_reminders", "apple_reminders.create_reminder", "gmail.gmail_search_threads", "gmail.gmail_read_thread", "gmail.gmail_create_draft", "weather.get_weather", "web.web_search", "web.fetch_page", "football.*", "brief.daily_brief", "timers.*", "training.*", "memory_tools.*", "delegate.delegate", "system.get_time", "maps.search_places", "maps.place_details", "maps.travel_time", "maps.geocode", "google_sheets.find_spreadsheet", "google_sheets.list_sheets", "google_sheets.read_range", "google_sheets.query_sheet", "google_sheets.append_rows", "google_sheets.update_range", "google_sheets.create_spreadsheet", "shortcuts.*", "listening.pause_listening", "power.mac_status", "power.lock_screen", "power.sleep_mac", "power.schedule_sleep", "power.cancel_scheduled_sleep", "alarms.*", "brief.set_brief_schedule"]`): Tools a remote (Telegram) turn may use: "module.tool" or "module.*". Everything else is removed from the model's tool list and refused in code. No shell, files, apps, screen, clipboard, Spotify, dev.

## [voice]

Hands-free voice service. `general.use_voice` must be true to start it.

`use_voice` in [general] must be true for `jarvis voice` to start. Everything runs on the Mac; nothing reaches the API before the wake word or the hotkey triggers.

- **`wake_word_model`** (string; default: `"hey_jarvis"`): openWakeWord pretrained model (hey_jarvis_v0.1.onnx)
- **`wake_word_threshold`** (number, 0 to 1; default: `0.5`): tune with `jarvis voice calibrate`
- **`wake_word_cooldown_s`** (number, >= 0; default: `2.0`): no second trigger this soon after a detection
- **`wake_word_barge_in`** (boolean; default: `false`): true (headphones): "Hey Jarvis" also interrupts Jarvis while it speaks
- **`post_speech_cooldown_s`** (number, >= 0; default: `1.0`): ignore the wake word this long after Jarvis finishes speaking
- **`hotkey`** (string; default: `"<alt>+<space>"`): hold to talk; press while Jarvis speaks to interrupt
- **`listen_sound`** (string; default: `"/System/Library/Sounds/Tink.aiff"`)
- **`no_speech_sound`** (string; default: `"/System/Library/Sounds/Pop.aiff"`)
- **`vad_silence_ms`** (integer, >= 100; default: `700`): silence that ends the recording
- **`vad_threshold`** (number, 0 to 1; default: `0.5`)
- **`max_record_s`** (integer, >= 1; default: `30`)
- **`no_speech_timeout_s`** (integer, >= 1; default: `5`): nothing said after the wake word: back to idle, no API call
- **`stt_model`** (string; default: `"mlx-community/whisper-small-mlx"`)
- **`stt_language`** (`"tr" | "en" | "auto"`; default: `"tr"`): Whisper decodes in this language and skips its per-utterance detection, which mistook one short Turkish request in four for English or another language (`jarvis voice debug-record` shows what it hears). "en" to speak English for a while; "auto" brings the detection back, limited to `stt_languages`.
- **`stt_model_by_language`** (table of strings; default: `{}`; example: `{ en = "mlx-community/whisper-small.en-mlx" }`): A different model when `stt_language` is one of these (English-only Whisper is smaller and better at English).
- **`stt_languages`** (list of strings, at least 1 entry; default: `["tr", "en"]`): auto mode: anything else detected falls back to the first entry
- **`stt_engine`** (`"apple" | "whisper" | "elevenlabs" | "hybrid"`; default: `"whisper"`; example: `"apple"`): The recognizer (`jarvis voice test-stt` compares them on your own voice): Apple's on-device Speech framework (free, nothing leaves the Mac, fast). "whisper" (stt_model above, also the automatic fallback when Apple fails), "elevenlabs" (Scribe v2: cloud, paid, the audio leaves the Mac) or "hybrid" (Apple, then Scribe when Apple's confidence is below stt_hybrid_threshold).
- **`stt_hybrid_threshold`** (number, 0 to 1; default: `0.6`)
- **`preroll_ms`** (integer, 0 to 2000; default: `1000`): audio kept from before the recording starts, so the first word is not cut
- **`stt_hallucination_blocklist`** (list of strings; default: `["Altyazı M.K.", "Thanks for watching!", "Thank you."]`; example: `["Altyazı M.K.", "Thanks for watching!", "Thank you.", "İzlediğiniz için teşekkür ederim.", "Abone ol"]`)
- **`tts_engine`** (`"say" | "elevenlabs"`; default: `"say"`): "elevenlabs" | "say"; `say` is always the fallback
- **`tts_voice_tr`** (string; default: `"Yelda"`): `say` voice (fallback): Enhanced/Premium is used automatically when installed
- **`tts_voice_en`** (string; default: `"Samantha"`): `say` voice for English (`say -v ?` lists them)
- **`tts_rate`** (integer, 80 to 400; default: `190`): words per minute for `say -r`
- **`elevenlabs_voice_id`** (string; default: `""`): ElevenLabs. Key: `jarvis voice set-elevenlabs-key` (Keychain, never here). from `jarvis voice list-voices`
- **`elevenlabs_model`** (string; default: `"eleven_flash_v2_5"`): lowest latency model with Turkish and English
- **`elevenlabs_first_chunk_timeout_s`** (number, > 0; default: `3.0`): no audio within this many seconds: this sentence falls back to `say`
- **`elevenlabs_monthly_char_budget`** (integer, >= 0; default: `100000`; example: `10000`): your plan's monthly characters (check your ElevenLabs plan); above it Jarvis switches to `say`
- **`elevenlabs_use_for_tainted`** (boolean; default: `true`): false: replies in tainted turns (email/web content) are spoken by `say`, not sent to ElevenLabs
- **`elevenlabs_text_normalization`** (`"on" | "auto" | "off"`; default: `"on"`): ElevenLabs' own number spelling as a safety net behind Jarvis's normalizer: "on" | "auto" | "off"
- **`confirm_phrases`** (list of strings, at least 1 entry; default: `["onaylıyorum", "evet onaylıyorum", "confirm", "yes confirm"]`): found as whole words in a short answer; "evet" alone is asked again; "hayır"/"iptal" deny
- **`confirm_timeout_s`** (integer, >= 3; default: `20`): the spoken answer expires this long after the question has finished playing (the dialog stays until then)
- **`pause_phrases`** (list of strings; default: `["sesi kapat", "dinlemeyi durdur", "stop listening"]`): Pause phrases, matched exactly in code and handled without the model (a duration may be added: "1 saat sesi kapat"). Pausing releases the microphone (the orange dot disappears) while the service keeps running; the same pause comes from `jarvis voice pause [--for 60m]`, Telegram /mute and the `pause_listening` tool. Back on: `jarvis voice resume`, /unmute, holding the hotkey (a dialog asks), or when the duration ends.
- **`follow_up_mode`** (`"always" | "questions_only" | "off"`; default: `"always"`): Follow-up mode: after a reply has been played to the end, Jarvis listens again for a short window without "Hey Jarvis" (a soft sound marks it). Speech that starts inside the window is recorded to its end and becomes the next turn; after that reply a new window opens, so a conversation flows until you stay silent. Silence or noise closes the window quietly. No window while paused; "sesi kapat" in a window pauses at once. The hotkey still works during the window; confirmations keep their own rules. "always" | "questions_only" (only after a reply that ends with "?") | "off"
- **`follow_up_window_s`** (number, 0.5 to 60; default: `6.0`): seconds to START talking after the reply; the speech itself may run longer
- **`show_transcript_notification`** (boolean; default: `false`): background mode: show what Jarvis heard as a macOS notification
- **`save_audio`** (boolean; default: `false`): true keeps every recording under data/voice_audio/ (debugging only)
- **`sounds`**: see [`[voice.sounds]`](#voicesounds).

### [voice.sounds]

Cue sounds under `<JARVIS_HOME>/sounds/` (`[voice.sounds]`). `heard` plays once a request has been recorded (non-blocking); `ready` plays before the follow-up window opens (the microphone waits for it). Names are file base names: `sounds/<name>.m4a|.mp3|.wav|.aiff`, first found wins; a macOS system sound plays when the file is missing.

Cue sounds from &lt;JARVIS_HOME>/sounds/ (see sounds/README.md): &lt;name>.m4a, then .mp3, .wav, .aiff; a macOS system sound plays when the file is missing (`jarvis doctor` warns). Played with `afplay`.

- **`heard`** (string; default: `"voice_heard"`): right after your request has been recorded (end of speech / hotkey release); non-blocking, stopped as soon as the reply's first audio starts
- **`ready`** (string; default: `"voice_ready"`): Jarvis finished speaking and listens again: the follow-up window (and its seconds) starts only after this cue has finished playing
- **`volume`** (number, 0.0 to 2.0; default: `1.0`): afplay -v (0 = silent, 1 = the file's own level)
- **`heard_enabled`** (boolean; default: `true`)
- **`ready_enabled`** (boolean; default: `true`)
- **`thinking`** (string; default: `"thinking_sound"`): loops quietly while Jarvis works on the answer (transcription, API, tools): starts after the heard cue once thinking_delay_ms passed without a spoken reply, stops at the first audio of the reply, a confirmation, an error, a barge-in or a pause
- **`thinking_enabled`** (boolean; default: `true`)
- **`thinking_volume`** (number, 0.0 to 2.0; default: `0.4`; example: `0.8`): its own afplay -v, lower than the cues
- **`thinking_delay_ms`** (integer, 0 to 10000; default: `700`; example: `200`): a reply that starts within this stays clean (no thinking sound at all)
- **`thinking_gap_ms`** (integer, 0 to 10000; default: `0`): silence between two loops of the file

## [sheets]

Google Sheets. `aliases`: a short name -> spreadsheet id, so "add this to my training sheet" works.

Google Sheets. Short names for spreadsheets, so "add this to my training sheet" works: `aliases = { "training" = "<spreadsheet id from the sheet's URL>" }`

- **`aliases`** (table of strings; default: `{}`)

## [maps]

Google Maps Platform. The API key lives in the Keychain (`jarvis key set google_maps_api_key`).

Google Maps Platform. Key: `jarvis key set google_maps_api_key` (Keychain, never here).

- **`open_with`** (`"apple" | "google"`; default: `"apple"`): "apple" | "google": which app `open_in_maps` opens
- **`default_mode`** (`"transit" | "driving" | "walking" | "bicycling"`; default: `"transit"`): travel_time default: "transit" | "driving" | "walking" | "bicycling"
- **`leave_buffer_min`** (integer, >= 0; default: `10`): "when should I leave": minutes added on top of the travel time
- **`daily_call_limit`** (integer, >= 0; default: `100`): Maps API calls per day (all APIs together); 0 disables the guard

## [brief]

- **`include_travel`** (boolean; default: `false`): true: the daily brief adds the travel time to the first event with a location
- **`include_mail`** (boolean; default: `true`): the brief lists the mail that reached the inbox today and names the important ones
- **`schedule`**: see [`[brief.schedule]`](#briefschedule).

### [brief.schedule]

The automatic morning brief (scheduler/brief.py), delivered once a day by the scheduler agent at `weekday_time` or `weekend_time` ("" or "off" = no brief on those days). `channel`: "auto" speaks it when the user is at the Mac (active within `active_within_min`, voice running, not paused, no Do Not Disturb) and sends it to Telegram otherwise; "voice" and "both" still fall back to Telegram when speaking is not possible. A brief missed while the Mac slept is delivered on wake until `late_until`, then skipped. A brief the user asked for that morning (`daily_brief`) also makes the automatic one skip.

The automatic morning brief: the scheduler agent delivers today's brief once a day, at weekday_time on Monday-Friday and at weekend_time on Saturday-Sunday ("off" = no brief on those days). channel: "auto" speaks it on the Mac when you are there (active within active_within_min minutes, voice service running and not paused, no Do Not Disturb) and sends it to Telegram otherwise; "telegram", "voice" or "both" force a channel (voice still falls back to Telegram when it cannot speak). If the Mac was asleep at the time, the brief comes on wake until late_until, later it is skipped. A brief you asked for yourself that morning ("morning brief", /brief) makes the automatic one skip. `jarvis brief schedule [on|off]` shows and toggles it; "move the morning brief to 7:30" or "turn the brief off" change it from the chat (config.local.toml).

- **`enabled`** (boolean; default: `false`)
- **`weekday_time`** (string; default: `"09:00"`)
- **`weekend_time`** (string; default: `"10:30"`)
- **`channel`** (`"auto" | "telegram" | "voice" | "both"`; default: `"auto"`): "auto" | "telegram" | "voice" | "both"
- **`late_until`** (string; default: `"12:00"`)
- **`active_within_min`** (integer, 1 to 240; default: `15`)

## [shortcuts]

Apple Shortcuts bridge. Only the listed Shortcuts can run.

Apple Shortcuts bridge. Jarvis runs only the Shortcuts listed below, through the macOS `shortcuts` CLI (argv, never a shell). `jarvis shortcuts list` shows every Shortcut on this Mac and marks the allowlisted ones; `jarvis doctor` reports which entries are missing. With an empty list the Shortcut tools are not offered to the model at all.

- **`timeout_seconds`** (integer, >= 1; default: `30`)
- **`allowed`**: see [`[[shortcuts.allowed]]`](#shortcutsallowed).

### [[shortcuts.allowed]]

An array of tables: each `[[shortcuts.allowed]]` block in the file adds one entry.

One Apple Shortcut Jarvis may run. `name` must match the Shortcuts app exactly.

- **`name`** (string, at least 1 character; *required*; example: `"Jarvis Location"`)
- **`description`** (string, at least 1 character; *required*; example: `"Returns the Mac's current location (latitude, longitude, address) for Jarvis's Current Location"`): the model matches requests against this
- **`risk`** (`"safe" | "confirm"`; default: `"confirm"`; example: `"safe"`): safe runs directly, confirm asks first
- **`remote`** (boolean; default: `false`): may run from Telegram
- **`taints`** (boolean; default: `false`): the output is untrusted (a Shortcut that reads a web page, for example)

## [network]

Internet test and history. Full speed tests use data and never run on their own unless `periodic_speedtest_hours > 0`; periodic quick checks (diagnostics only) are off by default.

Internet test: `internet_test` runs the diagnostics (interface, router, DNS, public hosts, Wi-Fi signal) and, with full = true, macOS's `networkQuality` speed test. Every result lands in the `network_tests` table (`internet_history`). Full speed tests use data: they never run on their own unless periodic_speedtest_hours > 0.

- **`periodic_check_min`** (integer, >= 0; default: `0`): 0 = off; else the scheduler runs a quick check (no speed test) every N minutes and notifies only when the internet goes down and when it comes back
- **`periodic_speedtest_hours`** (integer, >= 0; default: `0`): 0 = never run a full speed test automatically
- **`public_check_hosts`** (list of strings, at least 1 entry; default: `["1.1.1.1", "8.8.8.8"]`): "is the internet reachable" (ping + TCP 443/53)
- **`dns_check_names`** (list of strings, at least 1 entry; default: `["apple.com", "google.com"]`): "does DNS work"
- **`speedtest_max_runtime_s`** (integer, 5 to 120; default: `30`): cap for `networkQuality -M`

## [presence]

"Am I home?" and "Who is home?". Filled by `jarvis presence setup`.

"Am I home?" / "Who is home?". The home network is identified by the router's MAC address (the ARP entry of the default gateway), not by the Wi-Fi name: `jarvis presence setup` fills it in. People are detected by their phones' MAC addresses on the home Wi-Fi; scans run inside the scheduler agent every scan_interval_s, only while the Mac is on the home network, and probe only the devices listed below plus a light periodic ARP sweep. Presence data stays on this Mac.

- **`home_gateway_macs`** (list of strings; default: `[]`): personal: `jarvis presence setup` writes it to config.local.toml
- **`scan_interval_s`** (integer, >= 30; default: `120`)
- **`away_after_min`** (integer, >= 1; default: `10`): a person becomes "away" only after not being seen for this long (phones sleep their Wi-Fi)
- **`allow_remote`** (boolean; default: `false`): presence tools from Telegram: off, so a stolen phone cannot learn when the house is empty
- **`allow_remote_self`** (boolean; default: `false`): exception: only `am_i_home` (about you) from Telegram
- **`on_arrive_greet`** (boolean; default: `false`): when you arrive: Jarvis greets you by voice with a short brief (voice agent running, not paused)
- **`on_leave_pause_voice`** (boolean; default: `false`): when the Mac leaves the home network: pause voice listening; resume when it returns
- **`notify_person_changes`** (boolean; default: `false`): notification when a configured person arrives or leaves: on the Mac; also on Telegram (timers.notify_channels) only when allow_remote = true
- **`people`**: see [`[[presence.people]]`](#presencepeople).

### [[presence.people]]

An array of tables: each `[[presence.people]]` block in the file adds one entry.

One household member and the MAC addresses of their devices on the home Wi-Fi.

- **`name`** (string, at least 1 character, at most 64 characters; *required*)
- **`devices`** (list of strings, at least 1 entry; *required*): MAC addresses (an iPhone's private address must be "Fixed" for the home network)
- **`is_me`** (boolean; default: `false`)
- **`track_history`** (boolean; default: `true`): false: only the current state is kept, no arrivals/departures

## [location]

Current Location detection. Sources in order: the allowlisted Shortcut `shortcut_name` ("Get Current Location"), CoreLocationCLI when installed, IP geolocation (city level, approximate). The lookup runs in the background at session start and lazily when a location-dependent tool finds the stored location older than `max_age_min`.

Current Location (where you are now; the home `Location` in profile.md never changes). Looked up in the background at the start of every CLI and voice session and again when a weather/maps tool finds it older than max_age_min; `jarvis location` shows it, `jarvis location refresh` forces a lookup. Sources in order: the Shortcut below (must exist in the Shortcuts app and be allowlisted under [[shortcuts.allowed]]), CoreLocationCLI if installed (`brew install --cask corelocationcli`), IP geolocation (city level, marked approximate, wrong behind a VPN). Exact coordinates stay in data/location_state.json; profile.md (sent to the API on every request) gets only the label at profile_precision.

- **`enabled`** (boolean; default: `true`)
- **`refresh_on_start`** (boolean; default: `true`): background refresh at the start of every CLI / voice session
- **`shortcut_name`** (string; default: `"Jarvis Location"`): must also be under [[shortcuts.allowed]] (risk safe, remote false)
- **`timeout_s`** (number, > 0, <= 60; default: `5.0`): per source
- **`max_age_min`** (integer, >= 1; default: `60`): older than this: refresh before a weather/maps tool runs
- **`profile_precision`** (`"city" | "neighborhood" | "street"`; default: `"neighborhood"`): "city" | "neighborhood" | "street": what enters profile.md
- **`keep_history`** (boolean; default: `false`): true appends every new location to data/location_history.jsonl
- **`ip_fallback`** (boolean; default: `true`; example: `false`): true: approximate city from your IP address via ip_lookup_url (a third-party service)
- **`ip_lookup_url`** (string; default: `"https://ipinfo.io/json"`): JSON with city/region/country and loc or latitude/longitude

## [dashboard]

`jarvis dashboard`: the local monitoring and settings page, served on 127.0.0.1 only while the command runs in the foreground.

`jarvis dashboard`: the local monitoring and settings page in the browser. It runs only while the command runs in the terminal (Ctrl-C stops it), listens on 127.0.0.1 only and opens with a one-time link.

- **`port`** (integer, 1024 to 65535; default: `8765`): if the port is busy, the next free one is used
- **`idle_lock_min`** (integer, 1 to 240; default: `3`): the page locks after this many minutes without clicks, typing or scrolling (a banner warns one minute before)
- **`unlock`** (`"click" | "touch_id"`; default: `"click"`): "click": Continue unlocks at once; "touch_id": Continue asks for Touch ID (or the Mac password)
- **`doctor_refresh_s`** (integer, 2 to 600; default: `10`): how often the Overview re-runs the quick health checks
- **`backups_keep`** (integer, 1 to 200; default: `20`): data/backups/&lt;timestamp>/ folders kept by the save flow
- **`correction_words`** (list of strings; default: `["no ", "not that", "wrong", "i meant"]`; example: `["hayır", "hayir", "yok", "değil", "degil", "olmadı", "olmadi", "yanlış", "yanlis", "öyle değil", "demek istediğim", "no ", "not that", "wrong", "i meant"]`): Analytics "Corrections": a voice request that starts with one of these within two minutes of the previous one counts as a correction of it (the "Repeats" next to it need no words: the same request said again).
